surface_mechanism_description: The rapid SiO2 ALD process occurs via siloxane polymerization, where siloxane polymer chains grow at the Al-catalytic sites, and the cross-linking of these polymer chains forms a dense SiO2 film. The first exposure to TMA forms a layer of chemisorbed dimethyl aluminum oxide, which enables the ALD process to continue.
evidence: The rapid SiO2 ALD is believed to occur via siloxane polymerization [16]. Siloxane polymer chains grow at the Al-catalytic sites, and the cross-linking of these polymer chains forms a dense SiO2 film that can grow at rates up to 6 nm per cycle at 300 °C if sufficient TBS is provided. The first exposure to TMA, both surfaces form a layer of chemisorbed dimethyl aluminum oxide, which is the functionality that enables the rapid SiO2 ALD process to continue.
